Q: Ansible-lint output not displayed in Visual Studio Code A:

I suggest installing the Error Lens extension for VS Code. It should solve your problem by displaying diagnostics from Ansible Lint directly in the editor.

Q: SLF4J vs Log4j vs Logback: Architectural difference? A:

I use JUL in small projects sometimes but you usually pull SLF4J in as a dependency anyway once you start using any libraries

Q: Implementing a custom comparer that treats the numbers as integers rather than strings A:

Like Dale K, I'm puzzled as to where you got the idea that "Microsft" (I assume you mean C#/.NET specifically?) sorts numbers as text. If you have a list of numbers, the standard sort will sort them numerically.

The following code:

List<int> numbers = new List<int> { 1, 11, 2, 3, 10 };
numbers.Sort();

foreach (var number in numbers)
{
  Console.WriteLine(number);
}

will output

1
2
3
10
11

Live demo: https://dotnetfiddle.net/PxYQZW

You don't need a custom comparer for this task - the AI on DuckDuckGo that you linked to is hallucinating (or possibly not doing good enough research).

Of course if you had a list of strings then you'd get a different result:

List<string> numbers = new List<string> {"1", "11", "2", "3", "10" };
numbers.Sort();

foreach (var number in numbers)
{
  Console.WriteLine(number);
}

outputs

1
10
11
2
3

Live demo: https://dotnetfiddle.net/ejXn7e

Maybe this is a scenario you've been in at some point which led you the conclusion that numbers are always sorted as text??

You could use a custom comparer to change that output, but of course a far more sensible solution would be simply to have the list be of type int to begin with, as above.

Q: How do I get Git to show command-line help in Windows? A:

Issue 187 issue 696 does report:

The main problem is that we do ship neither man.exe nor the man pages. Otherwise, you could set help.format to 'man' in /etc/gitconfig.

So right now, this isn't possible...

As jamiebarrow adds in the comments:

You could also try installing man yourself

MinGW-get install msys-man.

man is also available as a Windows binary: (found via the MinGW FAQ). That page also has groff.

As mentioned in "Getting Started - Getting Help", those three commands invokes the man page, but only in its HTML version:

$ git help <verb>
$ git <verb> --help
$ man git-<verb>

git <verb> -h does not print the man page, only the short usage section (nothing to do with man)

Q: How do I get a single Texture2D from a Sprite Atlas? A:

Why would you load it as a single Sprite though?

If it is a SpriteAtlas then load it as such. See Load sprite atlases manually at runtime after which you can simply list all contained individual sprites using SpriteAtlas.GetSprites, filter by name with the overload taking an additional string or get a specific one (the first match) by name using SpriteAtlas.GetSprite.

The entire point of a SpriteAtlas is that it is packing multiple sprites together using a single texture!

=> There are no underlying individual textures anymore!

If you really want/need to go back to individual textures on runtime for whatever reason you can simply create a crop from the texture containing all the individual sprites using simply the same textureRect as the sprite does. See e.g. Image cropping in Unity. This will only work though if the texture you get back from this is actually read/write enabled - for this the according flag needs to be set in the SpriteAtlas Inspector settings.
